text:
sara-chen: quick runtime follow-up from today's all-hands. two asks: (1) timeline for kernel v5 canary and gating; (2) short-term ops mitigations for recent kv-cache eviction spikes impacting low-latency pools. collect replies here for a brief customer note.

jason-roberts: kernel v5 status: three perf gates left (kv-stability, tail-p99, mem-regression). if green, we plan a tiny us-west canary tomorrow AM, broad canary 48h later. gates: eviction_rate < 0.06 sustained, p99 delta < 8%, no OOMs. i'll post canary id when launched.

deploy-bot: Canary queued: kernel-v5 | id=canary-1749 | region=us-west-2 | status=queued.

anita-garcia: eviction spikes correlate with sudden long-prefix bursts that bypass prefix cache and force KV reshuffle. ops mitigation (no code): increase pool reserve and enable prefix_fold window. low-risk and reversible.

trevor-moss: batching note: dynamic microbatching reduces tail latencies. recommendation for affected pools: dynamic_microbatch=true, target_batch_size=28-32 (start 32). we'll add an auto-tune job next sprint.

maya-singh: added eviction/seq_len heatmap: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/runtime/eviction-heatmap. ping me for access.

anita-garcia: ops snippet to roll (per-pool):
```yaml
pool_override:
  reserve_fraction: "0.35"
  dynamic_microbatch: "true"
  target_batch_size: "32"
  prefix_fold_window_secs: "3600"
```
jason-roberts: kernel allocator tweak: bias toward smaller initial KV allocations when seq_len variance is high. low-risk flag included in v5. rollback: flip predictor flag to legacy. PR and canary link coming.

deploy-bot: Canary started: id=canary-1749 in us-west-2 | status=running.

sara-chen: thanks everyone. jason/anita/trevor please post PRs/runbook with rollback steps and the watchdog metrics by EOD Friday. i'll draft the customer-facing update after review and set a 30m follow-up to review canary telemetry. :calendar:
